definition_zh: 永远；永久；老是，不停地
definition_en: for all time in the future; again and again or constantly
core_image: 一条没有尽头的直线：时间一直往前延伸，停不下来
scene: 毕业典礼上，两位好朋友把名字刻在校门口的老树上，约定这份友情不会消失。They promised that their friendship would last forever.
sceneCN: 这里 forever 是「永远」的意思（第 1 个义项：时间上无限延续）；两个朋友把友情比作刻在树上的名字，认为它会一直延续下去。

pos.zh: 老是；不停地（常与进行时连用）

derivatives.zh: forever 的形容词化表达，义为「永恒的；永久的」
与 forever 同义的形容词，义为「永久的；不朽的」
eternal 的名词形式，义为「永恒；来世」

senses.title: For all future time
senses.definition: for all time in the future, without ending
senses.definitionCN: 在未来的所有时间里持续下去，没有终点。
senses.example: I will remember this trip forever.
senses.exampleCN: 我会永远记住这次旅行。
senses.why: The word joins for (during) with ever (always), so the core image is time stretching without an end.
senses.whyCN: forever 由 for（在……期间）加 ever（总是）构成，核心意象是时间被拉长、看不到尽头。

senses.title: Again and again; constantly
senses.definition: used to say that someone does something very often, often annoyingly
senses.definitionCN: 表示某人经常做某事，常带抱怨或调侃语气。
senses.example: My little brother is forever borrowing my phone.
senses.exampleCN: 我弟弟老是借我的手机。
senses.why: In modern spoken English, the idea of endless time was applied to endless repetition, so forever also means doing something all the time.
senses.whyCN: 现代口语把「时间没有尽头」引申到「动作反复不停」，于是 forever 又有了「老是、总在」的用法。

senses.title: For a very long time (hyperbole)
senses.definition: used for emphasizing that something takes a very long time
senses.definitionCN: 用于夸张地强调某事耗时极长，并非真的永远。
senses.example: The queue at the canteen took forever today.
senses.exampleCN: 今天食堂的队排得久死了。
senses.why: Because forever is the longest possible time, speakers stretch it hyperbolically to any long wait.
senses.whyCN: 因为 forever 是最长的时间单位，说话人用夸张手法把任何漫长的等待都说成 forever。

intro.en: Forever is a transparent English compound, first recorded in the Middle English period, built from two native words.
intro.cn: forever 是一个结构透明的英语复合词，首见于中古英语时期，由两个本土词拼接而成。

items.en: The first element, fore, meant 'before, in front of' and the second, æfre (later ever), meant 'always, at any time'.
items.cn: 第一个成分 fore 意为「在前、在先」，第二个成分 æfre（后来写作 ever）意为「总是、任何时候」。

items.en: The two words fused into the compound phrase 'for ever', recorded around the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 两个词在十三世纪前后融合成复合短语 for ever，见于中古英语文献。

items.en: The phrase was later written as one word 'forever', which is now the standard American spelling and common everywhere.
items.cn: 这个短语后来合并拼写为 forever，如今是标准的美式拼法，各地通用。

items.en: The repetitive sense 'constantly' developed in colloquial use, especially in British English with continuous tenses.
items.cn: 「不停地」这一义项在口语中发展出来，英国英语尤其常与进行时连用。

items.en: Hyperbolic uses like 'take forever' spread in everyday speech to describe long waits.
items.cn: take forever 之类的夸张用法在日常口语里流行开来，用来形容漫长等待。

note.en: Words near forever and words that also express endless time or endless repetition.
note.cn: 与 forever 形近或同样表达无限时间、无休止重复的词。

entries.definition: toward the front or ahead in time; similar spelling with the same for- beginning
entries.definitionCN: 向前或提前；与 forever 拼写相近、同样以 for- 开头，但意思完全不同。

entries.definition: to lose a right or prize as a penalty; begins with for- but is unrelated
entries.definitionCN: 因受罚而丧失权利或奖赏；以 for- 开头，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: to search widely for food or supplies; shares letters with forever by chance
entries.definitionCN: 四处搜寻食物或物资；与 forever 字母相近纯属巧合。

entries.definition: at all times; overlaps with the repetition sense of forever
entries.definitionCN: 总是；始终；与 forever 的「不停地」义项重叠。

entries.definition: for all time, in a formal or literary tone
entries.definitionCN: 永久地；语气正式、书面，与 forever 的「永远」义项相近。

entries.definition: continuously, without stopping
entries.definitionCN: 持续不断地；与 forever 的「老是」义项相近，语气较正式。

normalIntro.en: Five memory hooks based on the parts and everyday phrases of forever.
normalIntro.cn: 基于 forever 的构词成分和常用搭配的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Split forever into for + ever: 'during ever' means during all time.
normal.cn: 把 forever 拆成 for + ever：「在这段所有时间里」，自然就是永远。

normal.en: for- here is not the 'for the sake of' preposition but the old 'forward in time' element.
normal.cn: 这里的 for- 不是介词「为了」，而是古义「往前推时间」的成分。

normal.en: Remember the phrase 'last forever' with an old oak tree that outlives generations.
normal.cn: 记住搭配 last forever，联想一棵比几代人活得都久的古橡树。

normal.en: 'Take forever' is what a slow queue feels like: the wait has no end.
normal.cn: take forever 形容慢吞吞的排队：等待仿佛没有尽头。

normal.en: British style: 'He is forever losing keys' — forever before an -ing verb means again and again.
normal.cn: 英式用法：forever 放在动词进行时前表示「老是」，如 He is forever losing keys。

abstract.en: Picture a straight line with no right end drawn across the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一条画满整页纸、右端没有终点的直线。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hands never move because time itself stopped.
abstract.cn: 想象一个指针永远不动的钟，时间本身停住了。

abstract.en: Picture a song repeating on loop that you cannot switch off.
abstract.cn: 想象一首单曲循环、怎么也关不掉的歌。

examples.en: Nothing lasts forever, so enjoy the good days while they are here.
examples.cn: 没有什么是永恒的，所以在好日子还在时好好享受。

examples.en: The download is taking forever; I have been waiting for half an hour.
examples.cn: 下载慢得要命，我已经等了半个小时。

examples.en: She is forever reminding me to water the plants.
examples.cn: 她老是提醒我给植物浇水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拂藕」——轻轻拂开藕的丝，丝断丝连永远扯不完，就像 forever 的时间没有尽头。

root: forever 是本土复合词：for（古英语，指「向前推进的时间」）+ ever（古英语 æfre，指「总是、任何时候」）。字面即「在所有时间里」，引申为「永远」；口语中又把无限时间投射到无限重复的动作上，产生「老是」义。

sensesIntro.en: Forever moves from endless time to endless repetition to exaggerated long waits.
sensesIntro.cn: forever 从「无限的时间」走向「无休止的重复」，再走向夸张化的「漫长的等待」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: time stretched into a line that never ends
core.cn: 核心意象：时间被拉成一条没有尽头的直线

branches.en: A promise or state that continues through all time
branches.cn: 承诺或状态贯穿所有时间，永远持续

branches.en: Endless time mapped onto endless repetition of an action
branches.cn: 无限时间投射到动作的无休止重复上

branches.en: A habit complained about in the continuous tense
branches.cn: 用进行时抱怨某人的习惯性动作

branches.en: The longest time used as a ruler for any long wait
branches.cn: 把最长时间概念当作量尺，夸张地形容漫长等待

branches.en: Hyperbole turns eternity into everyday complaint
branches.cn: 夸张手法把「永恒」降格为日常抱怨用语

intro.en: Forever is a compound of two everyday English words, so its parts are easy to see.
intro.cn: forever 由两个日常英语词合成，成分一目了然。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root inside forever; related English compounds use the same native elements.
latinIntro.cn: forever 内部没有拉丁词根；英语中用同样本土成分构成的复合词可作参照。

items.meaningCN: 在时间上向前；持续期间
items.example: A forerunner runs ahead of the others.
items.exampleCN: forerunner 指「先行者」，for- 表示「在前」。

items.example: Ever since that day, we write to each other.
items.exampleCN: ever since 表示「自那以后一直」。

items.example: She never eats breakfast before noon.

items.exampleCN: everywhere 把「每个」加到「地点」上。

items.example: Everything in the fridge is fresh.
However hard it rained, we kept walking.
The hills seemed everlasting to the child.
items.exampleCN: everlasting 是 forever 的形容词化。
evergreen 由「总是」加「绿色」构成。

definition_zh: 忘记；忘掉；忘了带；不再想
definition_en: to fail to remember or keep in mind; to fail to bring something
core_image: 记忆像手里的沙子：一松手就漏光了
scene: 出门前，小明找了半天书包，才发现作业本还摊在书桌上。He was in such a hurry that he forgot to bring his homework.
sceneCN: 这里 forget 是「忘了做某事」（第 1 个义项：没有记住去做）；小明因为匆忙，脑子里根本没记住要带作业这件事。

collocations.zh: 忘记去做某事（事还没做）
忘记曾经做过某事（事已做过）

derivatives.zh: forget 加形容词后缀 -ful，义为「健忘的；常忘事的」
forgetful 的副词形式，义为「健忘地；常忘事地」
forgetful 的名词形式，义为「健忘；疏忽」
加否定前缀 un-，义为「难忘的；无法忘怀的」

senses.title: To fail to remember information or an action
senses.definition: to be unable to recall a fact, or to fail to remember to do something
senses.definitionCN: 想不起某件事，或没有记住要去做某事。
senses.example: I forgot her phone number, so I could not call her.
senses.exampleCN: 我忘了她的电话号码，所以没法给她打电话。
senses.why: The prefix for- means away, so forgetting is memory that falls away from the mind.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 for- 表示「离开」，所以忘记就是记忆从头脑中脱落。

senses.title: To fail to bring or take something
senses.definition: to fail to bring an object you intended to bring
senses.definitionCN: 本来打算带的东西，结果没有带。
senses.example: She forgot her umbrella on the train.
senses.exampleCN: 她把伞忘在火车上了。
senses.why: The mental slip extends to physical objects left behind.
senses.whyCN: 头脑中的疏忽延伸到实物：该带的东西被落下了。

senses.title: To stop thinking or caring about something
senses.definition: to put something out of your mind deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 有意把某事从心里放下，不再纠缠。
senses.example: Forget the argument and enjoy the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 别再想那场争吵，好好享受假期吧。
senses.why: Forgetting is also an act of letting go, not just a failure of memory.
senses.whyCN: 忘记不只是记忆失败，也可以是一种主动的放下。

intro.en: Forget is an Old English compound whose parts still mean exactly what they suggest.
intro.cn: forget 是一个古英语复合词，其组成部分的含义至今与直觉一致。

items.en: The verb getan meant 'to grasp, seize, obtain', the ancestor of modern get.
items.cn: 古英语动词 getan 意为「抓住、获得」，是现代 get 的祖先。

items.en: The prefix for- meant 'away, off', turning 'grasp' into 'lose one's grip'.
items.cn: 前缀 for- 意为「离开、脱落」，把「抓住」变成「抓不住」。

items.en: Forgietan therefore meant 'to lose hold of the mind', that is, to lose a memory.
items.cn: forgietan 因此意为「在头脑中失去持有」，也就是丢失一段记忆。

items.en: The word continued as forgetten, with the past forms forgot and forgotten settling down.
items.cn: 该词在中古英语中写作 forgetten，过去式 forgot 与过去分词 forgotten 逐渐定型。

items.en: The deliberate sense 'stop caring' and the derived word unforgettable developed in later centuries.
items.cn: 「不再想」的主动义项和派生词 unforgettable 在后世逐渐发展出来。

note.en: Words shaped like forget and words about losing memory.
note.cn: 与 forget 形近的词以及表示记忆丢失的词。

entries.definition: to stop being angry at someone; shares the for- prefix meaning 'away'
entries.definitionCN: 原谅；与 forget 共用表示「离开」的前缀 for-，同属古英语 for- 动词家族。

entries.definition: to abandon someone or something; another for- verb of Old English origin
entries.definitionCN: 抛弃；同样是带 for- 前缀的古英语动词，语义核心是「舍弃」。

entries.definition: the present participle of forget itself
entries.definitionCN: forget 的现在分词；提醒学习者本词的 -tt- 双写规律。

entries.definition: to leave out, especially from a list or text
entries.definitionCN: 省略、遗漏；比 forget 更书面，强调有意或无意地漏掉。

entries.definition: to fail to notice something
entries.definitionCN: 忽视、没注意到；强调观察层面的疏漏。

entries.definition: to fail to care for something properly
entries.definitionCN: 疏于照顾、忽视；强调该尽的责任没有尽到。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks built on the for- + get structure of forget.
normalIntro.cn: 基于 forget 的 for- + get 结构的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Break forget into for + get: you did not get the memory, so it is gone.
normal.cn: 拆成 for + get：「没拿到」记忆，自然就忘了。

normal.en: The for- prefix also appears in forgive and forsake: it marks letting go.
normal.cn: for- 前缀也出现在 forgive、forsake 中：都表示「放手、舍弃」。

normal.en: Use the contrast: remember to remember, forget to forget.
normal.cn: 用对反差记：remember 是「再抓一次」，forget 是「没抓住」。

normal.en: Note the double t in forgetting: short vowel before stress doubles.
normal.cn: 注意 forgetting 中 t 双写：重读闭音节前辅音字母要双写。

normal.en: Learn the pair 'forget to do' (not done) versus 'forget doing' (already done).
normal.cn: 记住 forget to do（还没做）与 forget doing（已做过）的差别。

abstract.en: Picture sand slipping through open fingers.
abstract.cn: 想象沙子从张开的手指间漏下去。

abstract.en: Picture a balloon flying away from your hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一个气球从你手中飞走。

abstract.en: Picture words on a whiteboard being wiped clean.
abstract.cn: 想象白板上的字被擦得一干二净。

examples.en: Do not forget to lock the door when you leave.
examples.cn: 离开时别忘了锁门。

examples.en: He forgot that the meeting had been moved to Friday.
examples.cn: 他忘了会议已改到周五。

examples.en: I will never forget the kindness my teacher showed me.
examples.cn: 我永远不会忘记老师对我的好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛给特」——连佛祖都特别给不了的记忆，说明你彻底忘了：forget 就是「抓不住」的记忆。

root: forget 来自古英语 forgietan：for-（偏离、失去）+ getan（抓住、获得）。字面义「失去持有」，即「丢失记忆」。与 forgive、forsake 同属古英语 for- 动词家族，都表示「放手」类动作。

sensesIntro.en: Forget moves from failed memory to abandoned objects to deliberate letting go.
sensesIntro.cn: forget 从「记忆失败」延伸到「该带的没带」，再到主动的「放下、不再想」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that fails to hold what it grasped
core.cn: 核心意象：一只抓不住东西的手

branches.en: A fact or action slips out of memory
branches.cn: 事实或要做的事从记忆中滑走

branches.en: Failure to remember an intended action
branches.cn: 没记住本来打算做的事

branches.en: The mental slip leaves a physical object behind
branches.cn: 头脑的疏忽让实物被落下

branches.en: Releasing a memory on purpose to feel lighter
branches.cn: 主动松开一段记忆，让心变轻松

branches.en: One image covers both losing and letting go
branches.cn: 同一个意象覆盖「无意丢失」与「有意放下」两端

intro.en: Forget shows the Old English for- prefix, which turns positive verbs into losing verbs.
intro.cn: forget 展示了古英语 for- 前缀：它把「得到类」动词变成「失去类」动词。

latinIntro.en: The for- family is Germanic, not Latin, so the comparison words below are native English verbs.
latinIntro.cn: for- 词族是日耳曼来源而非拉丁来源，因此对照词都选英语本土动词。

items.example: Forsake means to leave someone away from you.
items.exampleCN: forsake 中 for- 表示「离开」。

items.example: You get a letter from a friend.

items.meaning: to give away a debt of anger
items.example: She forgave her brother at once.
items.exampleCN: forgive 与 forget 同构：for- + 动词。

items.example: He would never forsake his friends.
Grandpa is a bit forgetful these days.
items.exampleCN: 形容词后缀 -ful 在此表「充满」。
双重后缀叠加：un- 否定 + -able 可被。

items.example: The old gate had been forgotten for years.

items.meaningCN: 记住；想起（拉丁来源的反义词）
items.exampleCN: remember 与 forget 构成核心反义对。

definition_zh: 叉子；餐叉；叉；岔路口；分叉
definition_en: a tool with pointed parts used for lifting food or breaking soil; a place where a road divides into two
core_image: 把一根主干分成两个方向：叉齿分开，道路分开
scene: 放学回家的路上，男孩走到那棵老槐树下，小路在这里分成了两条。At the old tree, the path forks into two smaller trails.
sceneCN: 这里 fork 用作动词，是「分叉」的意思（第 3 个义项：道路分成两条）；小路在老树处一分为二。

collocations.phrase: at the fork in the road

derivatives.zh: fork 加 -ed，义为「叉状的；分叉的」，如 forked tongue（蛇的分叉舌头）
fork 复合 lift，义为「叉车；铲车」

senses.title: An eating tool with points
senses.definition: a small tool with points used to pick up and eat food
senses.definitionCN: 带尖齿、用来叉取食物的小工具。
senses.example: She cut the steak and lifted a piece with her fork.
senses.exampleCN: 她切开牛排，用叉子叉起一块。
senses.why: The word names the shape first: the pointed prongs split into several tips.
senses.whyCN: 这个词首先命名的是形状：叉齿从一个柄分成好几个尖端。

senses.title: A farm or garden tool
senses.definition: a larger tool with points used for lifting hay or digging soil
senses.definitionCN: 齿更多更大、用来挑干草或翻土的农具。
senses.example: The farmer carried a pitchfork over his shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫肩上扛着一把干草叉。
senses.why: The same shape serves heavier work on the farm.
senses.whyCN: 同样的形状在农场里承担更重的活。

senses.title: A place where a road divides into two
senses.definition: a point where a road, path, or river divides into two branches
senses.definitionCN: 道路、小径或河流分成两条支线的地方。
senses.example: Turn left at the fork in the road.
senses.exampleCN: 在岔路口向左拐。
senses.why: The branching shape of the fork is mapped onto branching roads.
senses.whyCN: 叉子的分叉形状被映射到分岔的道路上。

senses.title: To divide into two; to lift with a fork
senses.definition: to divide into two parts, or to lift, pierce, or dig with a fork
senses.definitionCN: 分成两部分；用叉子叉起或翻动。
senses.example: The path forks just beyond the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 小路在桥那边不远处分叉。
senses.why: The noun's shape meaning becomes a verb of dividing or lifting.
senses.whyCN: 名词的「形状」义动词化，表示「分成两支」或「叉起」的动作。

intro.en: Fork came into English from Latin through Germanic languages, keeping its 'divided shape' meaning throughout.
intro.cn: fork 从拉丁语经日耳曼诸语言进入英语，「分叉的形状」这一含义一路保持。

items.en: The word furca meant a two-pronged wooden implement, used in farming.
items.cn: 拉丁语 furca 指有两齿的木制农具，用于农事。

items.en: Borrowed early into Germanic languages as forca, furku, before English existed as we know it.
items.cn: 早在英语成形前，该词已被日耳曼诸语言借入，作 forca、furku。

items.en: Old English adopted forca for the farm tool with points.
items.cn: 古英语借入 forca，指带齿的农用叉。

items.en: As eating utensils spread in Europe, fork extended to the table knife's partner.
items.cn: 随着餐具在欧洲普及，fork 扩展到餐桌上的餐叉。

items.en: The road sense and the verb uses developed from the image of dividing into points.
items.cn: 「岔路口」义和动词用法都从「分成齿尖」的意象发展而来。

note.en: Words that look like fork and words for divided or pointed shapes.
note.cn: 与 fork 拼写相近的词，以及表示分叉、尖齿形状的词。

entries.definition: shape or a document; one letter different from fork
entries.definitionCN: 形式；表格；与 fork 仅一字母之差，注意元音 o 与 or 的区分。

entries.definition: people of a group or nation; rhymes visually with fork
entries.definitionCN: 民众；与 fork 字母结构相近，发音却不同。

entries.definition: to do a job; shares the -ork ending with fork
entries.definitionCN: 工作；与 fork 共享 -ork 词尾，属常见 -ork 词族。

entries.definition: a part that divides off from a main road, river, or organization
entries.definitionCN: 分支；强调「从主干分出」的部分。

entries.definition: a place where roads meet or cross
entries.definitionCN: 交叉点、交汇处；比 fork 更强调「汇合」。

entries.definition: one of the pointed parts of a fork or plug
entries.definitionCN: 尖齿、叉齿之一；指 fork 的单个齿。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks linking the shape of fork to its table, farm, and road meanings.
normalIntro.cn: 把 fork 的形状与餐桌、农田、道路三重含义连起来的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Picture four points on a fork: the word even echoes the number.
normal.cn: 想象叉子上的四个尖齿：单词发音还暗合 four。

normal.en: Chain the meanings: fork at dinner, fork on the farm, fork on the road.
normal.cn: 串起三义：餐桌的叉、田间的叉、路口的岔。

normal.en: A forked tongue of a snake is the adjective image: split in two.
normal.cn: 蛇的分叉舌头是形容词 forked 的画面：一分为二。

normal.en: 'Fork out money' means money leaves your hand as food leaves a fork.
normal.cn: fork out（掏钱）中钱离开手，就像食物离开叉子。

normal.en: At a fork in the road, choose left or right like choosing which prong.
normal.cn: 在岔路口选左或右，就像选叉子的哪根齿。

abstract.en: Picture a river splitting into two streams around a stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河绕过石头分成两股水流。

abstract.en: Picture a tree trunk splitting into two thick branches.
abstract.cn: 想象一根树干分出两条粗枝。

abstract.en: Picture hay lifted high on a pitchfork at sunset.
abstract.cn: 想象夕阳下草叉高高挑起的干草。

examples.en: Could you bring me a fork and a spoon, please?
examples.cn: 请给我拿一把叉子和一把勺子好吗？

examples.en: Keep left when the road forks near the farmhouse.
examples.cn: 路在农舍附近分叉时，请靠左走。

examples.en: He had to fork out two hundred yuan for the repair.
examples.cn: 他不得不掏两百块钱修东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拂扣」——用叉子把食物轻轻扣住，拂一下就叉起来：fork 的齿就是扣住食物的爪。

root: fork 源自拉丁语 furca（两齿木叉），经日耳曼诸语言进入古英语（forca）。核心义是「一分为二的形状」；餐叉、农叉、岔路口、动词分叉都由这一形状义辐射而出。

sensesIntro.en: Fork radiates from a divided shape to tools, roads, and verbs of splitting.
sensesIntro.cn: fork 从「分叉形状」辐射出餐具、农具、岔路与「分裂」动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one stem splitting into pointed branches
core.cn: 核心意象：一根柄分出带尖的支枝

branches.en: The small pointed tool for eating
branches.cn: 餐桌上叉取食物的小工具

branches.en: The heavy pointed tool for farm work
branches.cn: 农场里挑草翻土的大叉

branches.en: A road dividing just like the tool's points
branches.cn: 道路像叉齿一样一分为二

branches.en: The shape becomes a verb of dividing
branches.cn: 形状义动词化：表示分叉动作

branches.en: Piercing food with the points as a verb
branches.cn: 动词义里用尖齿扎起食物

intro.en: Fork is a single borrowed root; its family lives in compounds rather than affixes.
intro.cn: fork 是单个借入词根；它的词族主要体现在复合词而非词缀上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestor furca left no deep Latin family in English, so the list focuses on compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁祖先 furca 在英语中没有深厚的拉丁同族词，因此下面聚焦复合词。

items.example: The snake showed its forked tongue.
items.exampleCN: 形容词化，描绘分叉形状。

items.example: He turned the hay with a pitchfork.

items.meaning: a vehicle that lifts loads on forks
a U-shaped tool giving a fixed note
items.example: The choir used a tuning fork.
items.exampleCN: 以叉形命名的乐器工具。

items.example: She forked out for the tickets.
The trail bifurcates at the rock.
items.exampleCN: bi-（二）+ 词根，与 furca 同源。
书面术语，直接来自拉丁词根。

latinEntries.meaning: a two-pronged fork or wooden implement

latinEntries.meaningCN: 恶棍，字面义「扛叉者」，指被绞架之叉架起来的贼

definition_zh: 形式；形状；表格；种类；形成；组成；养成
definition_en: the shape or type of something; a printed document with spaces to fill in; to make or begin to have a shape
core_image: 一团泥被捏出轮廓：无形的东西获得确定的形状
scene: 开学第一天，老师发下一张纸，让每个人填写姓名和班级。Please fill in this form with your name and class.
sceneCN: 这里 form 是「表格」的意思（第 3 个义项：需要填写的文件）；开学时人人都要填一张登记表。

derivatives.zh: form 加形容词后缀 -al，义为「正式的；外表的」
form 加 -ation，义为「形成；编队；构造」
义为「以前的；前者」，来自 form 的比较级形态
同根词，义为「公式；配方」
加前缀 re-，义为「改革；改良」
加前缀 in-，义为「告知；使成形于心中」

senses.title: The visible shape of something
senses.definition: the visible shape or outline of a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 人或物可见的轮廓和形状。
senses.example: In the fog we could see the form of a tall building.
senses.exampleCN: 雾中我们只能看到一座高楼的轮廓。
senses.why: The Latin root forma names shape itself, before any abstract use.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 forma 最初命名的是形状本身，先于一切抽象用法。

senses.title: A type or kind of something
senses.definition: a type or variety of something, especially in abstract contexts
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的类型或存在方式，尤用于抽象语境。
senses.example: Email is now a common form of communication.
senses.exampleCN: 电子邮件如今是常见的交流形式。
senses.why: Visible shape extends to the 'shape' of abstract things like activities or energy.
senses.whyCN: 可见的形状延伸到抽象事物的「形状」，比如活动或能量的形态。

senses.title: A printed document with blanks
senses.definition: a printed paper or web page with empty spaces for writing information
senses.definitionCN: 印有空白栏、供人填写信息的纸页或网页。
senses.example: Please fill in this form and sign at the bottom.
senses.exampleCN: 请填写这张表格并在底部签名。
senses.why: A form gives information a fixed shape, like a mold.
senses.whyCN: 表格给信息规定固定形状，像模具一样。

senses.title: To make, build, or begin to exist
senses.definition: to give something a shape, or to start to exist as a group or thing
senses.definitionCN: 使某物具有形状，或（群体、事物）开始形成。
senses.example: The students formed a line at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们在校门口排成一列。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: to produce form.
senses.whyCN: 名词转动词：去「制造」形状。

senses.title: To develop a habit or idea gradually
senses.definition: to develop a habit, idea, or judgement over time
senses.definitionCN: 习惯、想法或判断随着时间慢慢养成。
senses.example: Reading before bed helped her form good habits.
senses.exampleCN: 睡前阅读帮助她养成好习惯。
senses.why: Abstract forming happens slowly, as shapes emerge in nature.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的「形成」是缓慢发生的，正如自然界中形状的浮现。

intro.en: Form comes straight from Latin forma, one of the most productive roots in English.
intro.cn: form 直接来自拉丁语 forma，是英语中能产性最强的词根之一。

items.en: Forma meant shape, figure, or appearance, and also a mold or pattern.
items.cn: 拉丁语 forma 意为形状、轮廓、外貌，也指模具、样板。

items.en: A related root *dher- meant to hold or support, giving the sense of a fixed outline.
items.cn: 相关词根 *dher- 意为「持有、支撑」，引出「固定轮廓」的意味（重构形式）。

items.en: The word passed into Old French as forme in learned and everyday use.
items.cn: 该词进入古法语写作 forme，用于书面与日常。

items.en: English borrowed forme around the twelfth to thirteenth century in the shape sense.
items.cn: 英语在十二至十三世纪借入 forme，先表示形状。

items.en: The document sense, the verb uses, and the huge derived family all flourished in Modern English.
items.cn: 「表格」义、动词用法和庞大的派生词族都在现代英语中蓬勃发展。

note.en: Words that look like form and words about shape, type, and making.
note.cn: 与 form 形近的词，以及表示形状、种类、塑造的词。

entries.definition: an eating tool; differs from form by one final letter
entries.definitionCN: 叉子；与 form 仅词尾一字母之差。

entries.definition: a company, or solid and steady; a frequent confusion with form
entries.definitionCN: 公司；坚固的；与 form 极易混淆，注意元音不同。

entries.definition: starting point of movement; differs by one letter and position
entries.definitionCN: 从、来自；与 form 字母相同仅序不同，拼写陷阱词。

entries.definition: the outline or form of something
entries.definitionCN: 形状；与 form 的第 1 义项近义，更口语。

entries.definition: the way parts are arranged into a whole
entries.definitionCN: 结构；强调部分之间的组织。

entries.definition: a visible shape, especially of a body
entries.definitionCN: 轮廓；体型；与 form 的外形义相近。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks connecting form's shape core to its main uses.
normalIntro.cn: 把 form 的「形状」核心与主要用法连起来的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Forma in Latin means shape: every sense is a kind of shaping.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 forma 就是「形状」：每个义项都是某种「塑形」。

normal.en: A form of water is ice, liquid, or steam: three shapes of one thing.
normal.cn: 水的形式是冰、液、汽：同一事物的三种形态。

normal.en: A form on paper gives blanks their fixed shape.
normal.cn: 纸上的表格给空白规定了固定的形状。

normal.en: Form a line at school: people take the shape of a queue.
normal.cn: form a line：人排成队列的形状。

normal.en: Watch the trap pair: form (shape) versus from (source).
normal.cn: 注意易混对：form（形状）与 from（来自）。

abstract.en: Picture wet clay taking shape on a spinning wheel.
abstract.cn: 想象湿泥在转轮上渐渐现出轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture ice cubes freezing into square forms.
abstract.cn: 想象水冻成正方体的冰块。

abstract.en: Picture scattered students forming a neat line.
abstract.cn: 想象散乱的学生排成整齐的一列。

examples.en: Fill in the form and hand it back to me today.
examples.cn: 填好这张表格，今天交回给我。

examples.en: Water can exist in the form of ice, liquid, and steam.
examples.cn: 水可以以冰、液体和水蒸气的形式存在。

examples.en: The two countries formed a new trade partnership.
examples.cn: 两国组成了新的贸易伙伴关系。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛母」——佛母孕育形貌，众生皆有形：form 就是一切事物的「形」。

root: form 来自拉丁语 forma（形状、轮廓、模具），一般认为与词根 *dher-（持有、支撑）相关（重构形式）。经古法语 forme 进入中古英语。「形状→种类→表格→塑形动词」全部由「形」这一核心辐射。

sensesIntro.en: Form runs from visible shape to abstract type, to documents, to verbs of making.
sensesIntro.cn: form 从可见形状走向抽象种类，再到文书表格，最后成为「塑造」类动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shapeless matter taking on a definite outline
core.cn: 核心意象：无形之物获得确定的轮廓

branches.en: The outline a body shows to the eye
branches.cn: 肉眼看到的轮廓外形

branches.en: The shape of abstract things such as energy
branches.cn: 抽象事物（如能量）的形态

branches.en: A mold that gives written information a shape
branches.cn: 给书面信息塑形的模具，即表格

branches.en: Giving shape to things and groups
branches.cn: 给事物、群体赋予形状的动作

branches.en: Slow shaping inside habits and opinions
branches.cn: 在习惯与观点中缓慢进行的塑形

intro.en: Form is one of the most fertile Latin roots in English, spawning a whole family.
intro.cn: form 是英语中最高产的拉丁词根之一，孕育了庞大的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forma and its relatives supply both English derivatives and Latin cognates.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 forma 及其近亲既供给了英语派生词，也留下了拉丁同源词。

items.example: Fog hid the form of the tower.

items.exampleCN: 「有固定外形」引申为「讲究场合」。
in- 在此不表否定词义之外的反义。

items.meaning: the act or result of forming
items.exampleCN: 名词化：塑造的过程或结果。
trans-（穿过）+ 塑形 = 彻底改形。

items.meaning: one shape for all; same everywhere

items.exampleCN: forma 的小词形：「固定的小模子」。

items.example: The formative years of a child.

definition_zh: 幸运地；幸好；侥幸
definition_en: by good luck; luckily
core_image: 掉落的杯子刚好落进接住的网：危险擦身而过
scene: 爬山时天下起大雨，同学们正好走到半山腰的亭子里避雨。Fortunately, they had reached the shelter just before the storm.
sceneCN: 这里 fortunately 是「幸好」的意思（第 1 个义项：因运气好而避免坏事）；他们恰好赶在大雨前到了亭子。

derivatives.zh: fortunately 的形容词形式，义为「幸运的；侥幸的」
同根名词，义为「运气；财富；命运」
un- + fortunately，义为「不幸地；遗憾地」
mis- + fortune，义为「不幸；灾祸」

senses.title: By good luck
senses.definition: happening because of good luck, often preventing something bad
senses.definitionCN: 因运气好而发生，常指躲过了坏事。
senses.example: Fortunately, the fire was put out quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 幸好大火很快被扑灭了。
senses.why: The word comes from fortune, the turning wheel of luck, plus the adverb ending.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自 fortune（命运之轮）加副词后缀，核心是「运气转动」的意象。

senses.title: As luck would have it (sentence adverb)
senses.titleCN: 作为评注：幸好（句子副词）
senses.definition: used to comment on a whole sentence, showing relief
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首评注整句，表达「万幸、松了口气」的态度。
senses.example: Fortunately, nobody was in the building when it fell.
senses.exampleCN: 幸好楼塌的时候楼里没人。
senses.why: The adverb floats to the front of the sentence to judge the whole event.
senses.whyCN: 副词移到句首，对整个事件作出评判。

intro.en: Fortunately traces back to the Roman goddess of luck, Fortuna, through Latin and Old French.
intro.cn: fortunately 可追溯到罗马命运女神 Fortuna，经拉丁语和古法语传入英语。

items.en: Fortuna was the goddess of chance, and fors meant luck or chance.
items.cn: Fortuna 是掌管机运的女神，fors 意为「运气、机缘」。

items.en: Fortunatus meant made happy by luck, the base of fortunate.
items.cn: fortunatus 意为「被运气眷顾的」，是 fortunate 的基础。

items.en: The word entered Old French as fortune, covering luck and wealth.
items.cn: 该词进入古法语写作 fortune，兼指运气与财富。

items.en: English borrowed fortune and built fortunate, then added -ly for the adverb.
items.cn: 英语借入 fortune，派生 fortunate，再加 -ly 构成副词。

items.en: The sentence-initial use commenting on lucky outcomes became standard.
items.cn: 置于句首、对幸运结果作总评的用法成为标准。

note.en: Words shaped like fortunately and words about luck and chance.
note.cn: 与 fortunately 形近的词，以及表示运气、机缘的词。

entries.definition: by bad luck; the negative twin of fortunately
entries.definitionCN: 不幸地；fortunately 的否定孪生词。

entries.definition: a strong building for defence; shares letters but not the luck meaning
entries.definitionCN: 堡垒；与 fortunately 字母相近，但词义与运气无关。

entries.definition: giving ease; contains com- + fort, a different root
entries.definitionCN: 舒适的；含 com- + fort 词根，与幸运词源不同。

entries.definition: by good luck; the everyday synonym
entries.definitionCN: 幸好；日常同义词，语气更口语。

entries.definition: in a lucky or joyful way
entries.definitionCN: 幸运地；快乐地；可与 fortunately 互换但更强调愉悦。

entries.definition: as if arranged by a protecting power
entries.definitionCN: 似有天助地；书面语中表达「万幸」。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks built on fortune, the goddess, and the sentence use.
normalIntro.cn: 基于 fortune、命运女神与句子用法的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Remember the goddess Fortuna spinning her wheel of luck.
normal.cn: 记住命运女神 Fortuna 转动运气之轮。

normal.en: Fortune means luck: fortunate is lucky, fortunately is luckily.
normal.cn: fortune 是运气：fortunate 幸运的，fortunately 幸运地。

normal.en: Note the sentence pattern: Fortunately, no one was hurt.
normal.cn: 记住句式：Fortunately, no one was hurt（幸好无人受伤）。

normal.en: Contrast with unfortunately to lock in both words at once.
normal.cn: 与 unfortunately 对照，一次锁定两个词。

normal.en: Spot the family: fortune, fortunate, misfortune, fortunately.
normal.cn: 观察词族：fortune、fortunate、misfortune、fortunately。

abstract.en: Picture a wheel of fortune stopping on the winning color.
abstract.cn: 想象幸运轮盘停在中奖的颜色上。

abstract.en: Picture a net catching a falling cup just in time.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网及时接住了掉落的杯子。

abstract.en: Picture rain starting right after you step under a roof.
abstract.cn: 想象你刚进屋雨就开始下。

examples.en: Fortunately, the bus was late too, so we did not miss it.
examples.cn: 幸好公交车也晚点了，我们没错过。

examples.en: He fell off his bike, but fortunately he was not badly hurt.
examples.cn: 他从自行车上摔下来，所幸伤得不重。

examples.en: Fortunately for the team, their best player recovered in time.
examples.cn: 对全队来说幸运的是，最佳球员及时康复了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「福车呢提」——运气这辆福车恰好停在门口等着你：fortunately 就是「好运及时赶到」。

root: fortunately 来自拉丁语 fors / Fortuna（运气、命运女神），经古法语 fortune 进入英语；fortunate（幸运的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成。词根的意象是「命运之轮转到好的一面」。

sensesIntro.en: Fortunately covers both lucky events and the speaker's relieved comment on them.
sensesIntro.cn: fortunately 既描述「因好运而发生的事」，也承载说话人「幸好、松了口气」的总评语气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the wheel of luck stopping on the good side
core.cn: 核心意象：命运之轮恰好转到好的一面

branches.en: A bad event was avoided by luck
branches.cn: 坏事因运气被躲过

branches.en: A good result arrived just in time
branches.cn: 好结果及时到来

branches.en: The whole sentence is marked as lucky
branches.cn: 副词给整句话盖上「幸好」的标记

branches.en: Speaker relief at a near miss
branches.cn: 说话人对擦身而过的危险的庆幸

branches.en: From event luck to commenting luck
branches.cn: 从「事件幸运」到「评注幸运」的延伸

intro.en: Fortunately is built with clear layers: fortune + -ate + -ly.
intro.cn: fortunately 结构层次清晰：fortune + -ate + -ly。

latinIntro.en: The root belongs to Latin fors and Fortuna, with Old French as the carrier.
latinIntro.cn: 词根属于拉丁语 fors 与 Fortuna，古法语是传入的桥梁。

items.example: She told her fortune with cards.
A fortuitous meeting changed his life.

items.exampleCN: 提示：此 fort 非彼 fort。

definition_zh: 四十；四十个；四十年代
definition_en: the number forty; the age or years from forty to forty-nine
core_image: 四捆各十根的小木棍排成一排：四十根一眼数得清
scene: 运动会上，爷爷说他在这个年纪才第一次跑完马拉松。My grandpa ran his first marathon when he was forty.
sceneCN: 这里 forty 是「四十（岁）」的意思（第 1 个义项：数目四十）；爷爷说自己四十岁时才完成首个马拉松。

derivatives.zh: forty 的序数词形式，义为「第四十」
forty 复合 -fold，义为「四十倍地」

senses.title: The number forty
senses.definition: the number between thirty-nine and forty-one
senses.definitionCN: 三十九和四十一之间的整数。
senses.example: There are forty students in our class.
senses.exampleCN: 我们班有四十个学生。
senses.why: The Old English form feowertig literally meant four tens.
senses.whyCN: 古英语形式 feowertig 字面意思就是「四个十」。

senses.title: A person's forties; the forties decade
senses.definition: the years of someone's life or a decade from forty to forty-nine
senses.definitionCN: 人生或年代中从四十到四十九的区间。
senses.example: She is in her forties but looks much younger.
senses.exampleCN: 她四十多岁，但看起来年轻得多。
senses.why: The number stretches into a range of years.
senses.whyCN: 数目延伸为一个年龄或年代的区间。

senses.title: A fixed quantity in phrases
senses.definition: a conventional number used in idioms and set phrases
senses.definitionCN: 习语和固定短语中约定俗成的数目。
senses.example: He closed his eyes for forty winks after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午饭后他闭眼小睡了一会儿。
senses.why: Languages love round numbers in idioms, and forty is the biblical example number.
senses.whyCN: 语言偏爱在习语里用整数，四十是《圣经》里的典型例数（如四十天大水）。

intro.en: Forty goes back to Old English counting, built from four plus a group-of-ten word.
intro.cn: forty 源自古英语的计数方式，由「四」加「十个一组」的词构成。

items.en: Feowertig combined feower (four) with -tig (a group of ten).
items.cn: feowertig 由 feower（四）加 -tig（十个一组）组合而成。

items.en: -tig was itself an old word for ten, later a number-forming suffix.
items.cn: -tig 本身是古老的「十」，后来变成造数词后缀。

items.en: The form became fourty, still spelling the word with u.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 fourty，还带着 u 的拼写。

items.en: In the seventeenth century the u was dropped and forty became the standard spelling.
items.cn: 十七世纪 u 被去掉，forty 成为标准拼法。

items.en: Idiomatic uses like forty winks and the forties settled in modern times.
items.cn: forty winks、the forties 等习语用法在近代定型。

note.en: Words that look like forty and related number words.
note.cn: 与 forty 形近的词及相关的数词。

entries.definition: the number ten plus four; often confused with forty
entries.definitionCN: 十四；与 forty 同含四个相似字母，重音与词序不同，极易混淆。

entries.definition: the base number inside forty
entries.definitionCN: 四；forty 的构成基数。

entries.definition: to lose as a penalty; starts with similar letters
entries.definitionCN: 罚失；与 forty 开头字母相近，词义无关。

entries.definition: the ordinal after forty-ninth
entries.definitionCN: 第五十；相邻的序数词。

entries.definition: the neighbouring tens number
entries.definitionCN: 三十；数列上的邻居。

entries.definition: twenty, used in older counting like four score
entries.definitionCN: 二十；旧式计数单位，四个 score 即八十。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the four-ten build and the spelling trap of forty.
normalIntro.cn: 围绕「四 + 十」构造与 forty 拼写陷阱的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Forty = four tens; no u in the spelling, unlike four.
normal.cn: forty = 四个十；拼写里没有 u，与 four 不同，这是最大的拼写陷阱。

normal.en: Chain the family: four, fourteen, forty, fortieth.
normal.cn: 串起词族：four、fourteen、forty、fortieth。

normal.en: In her forties means between forty and forty-nine years old.
normal.cn: in her forties 指四十到四十九岁之间。

normal.en: Forty winks is a short nap, a fixed idiom to remember as a whole.
normal.cn: forty winks 是固定习语「打个盹」，整体记忆。

normal.en: Mark the contrast: fourteen (10+4) versus forty (4x10).
normal.cn: 对比记忆：fourteen 是十加四，forty 是四个十。

abstract.en: Picture four bundles, each with ten sticks.
abstract.cn: 想象四捆木棍，每捆十根。

abstract.en: Picture a runner finishing a marathon at age forty.
abstract.cn: 想象一位四十岁的选手跑完马拉松。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar page for the nineteen-forties.
abstract.cn: 想象一页二十世纪四十年代的日历。

examples.en: The school library holds forty thousand books.
examples.cn: 学校图书馆藏书四万册。

examples.en: My aunt is in her forties and still travels every year.
examples.cn: 我姑姑四十多岁，仍每年旅行。

examples.en: He took forty winks before the evening shift.
examples.cn: 上晚班前他小睡了一会儿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「缚梯」——把四十级台阶缚成一架梯子，四级一组、每组十级：forty 就是四个十。

root: forty 源自古英语 feowertig：feower（四）+ -tig（十，后缀化）。中古英语作 fourty，十七世纪起省去 u 定型为 forty。词根结构是「四个十」的直接拼合。

sensesIntro.en: Forty runs from the exact number to age ranges to idiomatic fixed quantities.
sensesIntro.cn: forty 从精确数目延伸到年龄区间，再进入习语中的固定量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four bundles of ten counted at a glance
core.cn: 核心意象：四捆十件、一眼数尽的量

branches.en: The exact count between thirty-nine and forty-one
branches.cn: 三十九与四十一之间的精确计数

branches.en: A stretch of life years around forty
branches.cn: 以四十为中心的人生阶段

branches.en: A decade named by its tens number
branches.cn: 以十位数字命名的年代

branches.en: A symbolic number inside set phrases
branches.cn: 习语中的象征性数字

branches.en: From precise counting to conventional counting
branches.cn: 从精确计数到约定俗成的计数

intro.en: Forty is a native compound: a number word plus an old ten-suffix.
intro.cn: forty 是本土复合词：数词加古老的「十」后缀。

latinIntro.en: The number family is Germanic, so there are no Latin cognates; the suffix family is the study focus.
latinIntro.cn: 数词家族属日耳曼来源，无拉丁同源词；学习重点是 -tig 后缀家族。

items.exampleCN: -tig 后缀化后产出二十到九十。

definition_zh: 向前；前进；提前； forwards 的形容词：前面的；先锋的；发送；转交
definition_en: toward the front or ahead in time; situated in front; to send something on to another person
core_image: 身体前倾迈步：重心移向正前方
scene: 足球课上，教练大声指挥队员把球传向球门方向。The coach shouted, 'Pass the ball forward!'
sceneCN: 这里 forward 是「向前」的意思（第 1 个义项：朝前移动）；教练要求队员把球传向对方球门方向。

derivatives.zh: forward 加名词后缀，义为「早熟；冒进」
forward 加 -ly，义为「在前方；冒失地」
forward 的英式变体，义为「向前」，副词专用
反义方位词，义为「之后；后来」

senses.title: Toward the front in space or time
senses.definition: toward a place or time ahead of the present position
senses.definitionCN: 朝空间前方或时间前方移动。
senses.example: Please move forward so others can get on the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 请往前走，让别人能上车。
senses.why: For- means forward in time or front, and -ward marks direction.
senses.whyCN: for- 表示「在先、在前」，-ward 后缀标记方向。

senses.title: Situated near the front; advanced
senses.definition: placed near the front, or developing earlier than usual
senses.definitionCN: 位置靠前的，或发展得比一般早的。
senses.example: The forward engine of the plane took the impact.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机前部的发动机承受了撞击。
senses.why: The direction word becomes a position word.
senses.whyCN: 方向词变成位置词。

senses.title: To send on to another address or person
senses.definition: to pass a letter, message, or email on to someone else
senses.definitionCN: 把信件、消息或电子邮件转给别人。
senses.example: I forwarded your message to the class group.
senses.exampleCN: 我把你的消息转发到了班级群。
senses.why: Pushing something forward reaches the next person.
senses.whyCN: 把东西往前送，就送到了下一个人手里。

senses.title: A player who leads the attack
senses.definition: in sports, a player who plays near the opponent's goal
senses.definitionCN: 球类运动中靠近对方球门、主攻得分的队员。
senses.example: He plays as a forward in the school football team.
senses.exampleCN: 他在校足球队里踢前锋。
senses.why: The attacker stands forward of the team, closest to the goal.
senses.whyCN: 进攻队员站在全队最前方、离球门最近的位置。

intro.en: Forward is a native English compound of for- and -ward, two very old direction elements.
intro.cn: forward 是本土复合词，由 for- 与 -ward 两个极古老的方位成分构成。

items.en: For- meant 'in front, going before', seen in forefather and foremost.
items.cn: for- 意为「在前、先行」，见于 forefather、foremost。

items.en: -weard meant 'turned toward', the ancestor of -ward.
items.cn: -weard 意为「转向」，是 -ward 的祖先。

items.en: Foreweard meant the front part or earlier period.
items.cn: foreweard 指前部或更早的时期。

items.en: Forward and forwards split uses: adjective and verb favored forward, pure adverb often forwards.
items.cn: forward 与 forwards 分工：形容词、动词多用 forward，纯副词常见 forwards。

items.en: The email sense and business senses like look forward to became universal.
items.cn: 转发邮件义和 look forward to 等商务用法普及开来。

note.en: Words that look like forward and words of direction and sending.
note.cn: 与 forward 形近的词及表示方向、转发的词。

entries.definition: the adverb twin of forward, preferred in British English
entries.definitionCN: 向前；forward 的副词孪生形，英式英语更常用。

entries.definition: an introduction to a book; often confused with forward
entries.definitionCN: 书的序言；与 forward 仅一字母之差，易混。

entries.definition: a prize; shares the -ward ending but not the for- part
entries.definitionCN: 奖品；共享 -ward 词尾，与 forward 词义不同。

entries.definition: in front or earlier
entries.definitionCN: 在前面；提前；与 forward 的方向义近义。

entries.definition: continuing forward in time or space
entries.definitionCN: 继续向前；同含 -ward 后缀。

entries.definition: to pass on a message
entries.definitionCN: 转达、传递；与 forward 的转发义近义。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on direction, position, and the look forward to pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 围绕方向、位置与 look forward to 句式的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Split forward into for (front) + ward (toward): moving to the front.
normal.cn: 拆成 for（前）+ ward（朝向）：朝前方移动。

normal.en: Learn the fixed pattern: look forward to + doing.
normal.cn: 记住固定句式：look forward to + 动名词。

normal.en: Distinguish foreword (a book's preface) from forward (ahead).
normal.cn: 区分 foreword（序言）与 forward（向前）。

normal.en: In football, the forward is the front player nearest the goal.
normal.cn: 足球里 forward 是离球门最近的前锋。

normal.en: Forward an email = push the message onward to the next person.
normal.cn: 转发邮件就是把消息继续往前送。

abstract.en: Picture a runner leaning forward before the starting gun.
abstract.cn: 想象发令枪响前前倾起跑的选手。

abstract.en: Picture an envelope passed hand to hand along a line.
abstract.cn: 想象信封沿一排人手手相传。

abstract.en: Picture a clock hand jumping forward one hour.
abstract.cn: 想象时针向前拨快一小时。

examples.en: We are all looking forward to the school trip next week.
examples.cn: 我们都很期待下周的学校旅行。

examples.en: Could you forward this email to the head teacher?
examples.cn: 你能把这封邮件转发给校长吗？

examples.en: The car rolled slowly forward along the narrow lane.
examples.cn: 汽车沿着窄巷缓缓向前滚动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「福特德」——福特车向前开：forward 就是车头所指的方向。

root: forward 为古英语复合词：for-（前、先，见 forefather）+ -weard（朝向，见 -ward）。字面即「朝前」。英式副词变体 forwards；同根方位词有 backward、onward、afterward。

sensesIntro.en: Forward spans direction, position, transmission, and the attacking player role.
sensesIntro.cn: forward 横跨方向、位置、转发传递与球类运动的前锋角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: body weight shifting toward what is ahead
core.cn: 核心意象：重心移向前方

branches.en: Movement toward the front in space
branches.cn: 空间上朝前方移动

branches.en: Moving an event to an earlier time
branches.cn: 把事情提前到更早的时间

branches.en: Standing at the front of a group or machine
branches.cn: 位于群体或机器的前部

branches.en: Pushing a message onward to the next person
branches.cn: 把消息继续传给下一个人

branches.en: The front position in an attacking line-up
branches.cn: 进攻阵容中的最前位置

intro.en: Forward combines the front element for- with the direction suffix -ward.
intro.cn: forward 由「前」成分 for- 与方向后缀 -ward 组合而成。

latinIntro.en: The -ward family is Germanic, so the cognates are all native direction words.
latinIntro.cn: -ward 词族属日耳曼来源，同源词都是英语本土方位词。

items.example: A forefather is one who came before.

items.exampleCN: 副词加 -s 的英式习惯。

items.example: The author wrote a short foreword.
items.exampleCN: 与 forward 同源成分、不同含义。

items.example: I look forward to seeing you.

definition_zh: 建立；创立；创办（find 的过去式、过去分词：找到）
definition_en: to start or establish something such as a school, company, or city
core_image: 往地里打下第一根桩：建筑、组织从这一刻立起来
scene: 校庆典礼上，老校友指着石碑讲起学校的起源。The school was founded more than eighty years ago.
sceneCN: 这里 found 是「创立」的意思（第 1 个义项：创办机构）；学校是八十多年前建立的。

collocations.zh: 创立于二十世纪九十年代的慈善机构

derivatives.zh: found 加 -er，义为「创始人；创立者」（另义「沉没」的 founder 是不同动词）
义为「基础；地基；基金会；创立」
foundation 加 -al，义为「基础的；根本的」
co- + founder，义为「共同创始人」

senses.title: To establish an organization or place
senses.definition: to bring an institution, company, or city into existence
senses.definitionCN: 使机构、公司或城市开始存在。
senses.example: Her grandfather founded a small hospital in the town.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖父在镇上创办了一家小医院。
senses.why: The Latin fundare meant to lay a bottom or base, and founding is laying the first base of an organization.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fundare 意为「打基础」，创立组织就是给它打第一层地基。

senses.title: To base something on a principle
senses.definition: to base a belief, action, or decision on something
senses.definitionCN: 让信念、行动或决定以某物为依据。
senses.example: The verdict was founded on solid evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 判决建立在确凿的证据之上。
senses.why: The base image works for ideas as well as buildings.
senses.whyCN: 地基意象同样适用于抽象的观念。

senses.title: Past form of find
senses.titleCN: find 的过去式与过去分词
senses.definition: the past and participle of find, meaning discovered
senses.definitionCN: find 的过去式/过去分词，表示「找到」。
senses.example: I found my lost pen under the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 我在桌子底下找到了丢的钢笔。
senses.why: This is a different verb: find, found, found, sharing the shape but not the origin.
senses.whyCN: 这是另一个动词 find 的变形，与「创立」的 found 同形不同源。

intro.en: Found the verb to establish and found the past of find are two separate words that only look alike.
intro.cn: 「创立」的 found 与 find 的过去式 found 是两个词源完全不同的词，只是外形相同。

items.en: Fundare meant to lay a bottom, from fundus, the bottom or base.
items.cn: fundare 意为「打基础」，来自 fundus（底、基础）。

items.en: The word entered Old French as fonder, used for founding churches and cities.
items.cn: 该词进入古法语作 fonder，用于创建教堂与城市。

items.en: English borrowed fonden in the thirteenth century for establishing institutions.
items.cn: 英语十三世纪借入 fonden，用于创立机构。

items.en: Separately, the verb findan (to come upon) had the past form funde, ancestor of the other found.
items.cn: 另一边，古英语动词 findan（碰上、发现）的过去式 funde 是「找到」义 found 的祖先。

items.en: The two words merged in spelling but kept their different families: founder, foundation versus find, finder.
items.cn: 两词拼写合一但词族分明：founder、foundation 属一方，find、finder 属另一方。

note.en: Words that look like found and words about beginnings and bases.
note.cn: 与 found 形近的词及表示起点、根基的词。

entries.definition: a person who establishes something; also a verb meaning to sink or fail
entries.definitionCN: 创始人；另有「沉没、失败」义的动词，是同形不同源词。

entries.definition: a sum of money set aside; from Latin fundus, related to founding
entries.definitionCN: 基金；资金；与 found 同出拉丁 fundus。

entries.definition: a factory where metal is cast; from French fonderie
entries.definitionCN: 铸造厂；来自法语 fonderie，属同根词。

entries.definition: to set up permanently
entries.definitionCN: 设立；建立；与 found 的创办义近义。

entries.definition: to start a business or organization
entries.definitionCN: 创办；口语化说法。

entries.definition: to start or introduce a system or rule
entries.definitionCN: 制定；设立；语气正式。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks separating the two founds and fixing the founder family.
normalIntro.cn: 区分两个 found 并锚定 founder 词族的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Found (create) comes from Latin fundus, the bottom: you lay the base first.
normal.cn: 创立义的 found 出自拉丁 fundus（底）：先打地基再建楼。

normal.en: The other found is simply find in the past: find, found, found.
normal.cn: 另一个 found 就是 find 的过去式：find、found、found。

normal.en: Foundation has three faces: base, establishment, and charity fund.
normal.cn: foundation 一词三面：地基、创立、基金会。

normal.en: A founder is one who lays the base of a company.
normal.cn: founder 就是给公司「打地基」的人。

normal.en: Be founded on means built on a principle, like a building on stone.
normal.cn: be founded on 指以某原则为基础，如楼立于石。

abstract.en: Picture a builder hammering the first stake into soil.
abstract.cn: 想象建造者把第一根桩打进土里。

abstract.en: Picture a stone foundation under a rising school gate.
abstract.cn: 想象校门下方正在垒砌的石头地基。

abstract.en: Picture hands brushing dust off a found wallet.
abstract.cn: 想象双手拂去拾获钱包上的灰尘。

examples.en: The charity was founded by a group of retired teachers.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构由一群退休教师创办。

examples.en: Their friendship is founded on many years of trust.
examples.cn: 他们的友谊建立在多年的信任之上。

examples.en: She found the ticket she thought she had lost.
examples.cn: 她找到了本以为丢了的那张票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「防倒的」——地基打得好才能防倒：found 创立，先立防倒的根基。

root: found（创立）来自拉丁语 fundare「打基础」，词根 fundus「底」；经古法语 fonder 进入英语。与 find 的过去式 found 仅同形不同源。同根词：foundation（基础）、founder（创始人）、fund（资金）。

sensesIntro.en: Found moves from laying a physical base to establishing institutions and abstract bases, beside its twin past of find.
sensesIntro.cn: found 从「打地基」到「创办机构」，再到「抽象根基」；旁边还站着同形的 find 过去式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first stone laid under everything that follows
core.cn: 核心意象：垫在一切之上的第一块石头

branches.en: Starting a school, company, or city
branches.cn: 创办学校、公司或城市

branches.en: The person who lays the base is the founder
branches.cn: 打地基的人即创始人

branches.en: Ideas stand on evidence as on stone
branches.cn: 观念立于证据，如楼立于石

branches.en: Decisions founded on principles
branches.cn: 决定以原则为根基

branches.en: The unrelated twin: past of find
branches.cn: 无关的孪生词：find 的过去式

intro.en: Found heads a Latin family about bottoms, bases, and beginnings.
intro.cn: found 统领一个关于「底、基、始」的拉丁词族。

latinIntro.en: The root fundus gives English both the establish family and the money family.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 fundus 在英语中同时衍生「创立」族与「资金」族。

items.example: The fundus of a cup is its base.
They found a new club this year.
The founder opened the first shop.
He asked for a full refund.
She is the co-founder of the app.

items.meaning: place where metal is founded or cast
items.example: Iron was melted in the foundry.

latinEntries.meaningCN: 底；基础；（作为基底的）田产

latinEntries.meaning: to lay a bottom or foundation

definition_zh: 四；四个；四岁；四点钟
definition_en: the number four; a group of four people or things; the age or time of four
